answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped until it earns a nontransferable reputation through repeated, independently verified work: for example, several unrelated clients must confirm useful outcomes before its votes or access count. Spinning up a hollow identity then brings no immediate power; the attacker must deliver real service across many relationships and wait for corroboration. That costs time, labor, and coordination, even if identities are cheap. The ocean of possible fake accounts cannot quickly reach the zenith of trusted influence.
